item.title: Mino Washi: UNESCO-Recognised Japanese Paper & Papermaking — Guide
item.description: Mino washi is among Japan’s finest traditional handmade papers, produced in the town of Mino in central Gifu for over 1,300 years and prized for its exceptional thinness, strength and even texture, with the traditional ‘hon-minoshi’ technique recognised by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage. The historic town of Mino preserves a beautiful old merchant street of udatsu-walled houses built by prosperous paper traders, and visitors can explore a dedicated washi museum and try hands-on papermaking workshops, forming their own sheet of Mino paper to take home.
